1153: Pt–Rh by Saengdeejing's method (CALPHAD route): a TDB built from MACE-MPA-0 (2026-11-11)
1154: For the user's request "draw the Pt–Rh phase diagram by Saengdeejing's method, the MLIP is Claude's choice", MACE-MPA-0 was chosen (its 0 K ordering energies are closest to DFT, and it is the only MLIP with both defect-cell and CE+MC results) and the procedure of the paper's Table 6 and eqs. 11–15 was reproduced with pycalphad (ptrh/calphad_params.py → calphad_tdb.py → calphad_figure.py, output ptrh/out/calphad_mace_mpa_0/, README result 8). Pure elements are SGTE91 (espei.refdata). fcc is ideal mixing + Redlich–Kister with ⁰L = −6084 + 2.60 T, ¹L = +477 + 0.32 T, ²L = −226 − 1.19 T J/mol (a from the 0 K mixing enthalpy of the 32-atom random cells, 13 compositions × 2 configurations; b from the 300–1000 K slope of the excess harmonic-phonon free energy of the same cells; the paper has −8725 + 4.53 T for PFP and −5000 + 1.3 T for DFT). The ordered phases PtRh (I4₁/amd) and D0₂₂ (PtRh₃, Pt₃Rh) are the paper's unpartitioned two-sublattice CEF, mixed end-members = Neumann–Kopp sum + ΔH_f − TΔS_f (ΔH_f −26.8 / −19.7 / −16.6 meV/atom, ΔS_f −0.154 / −0.087 / −0.080 k_B; paper PFP −37.6 / −28.0 / −23.5, DFT −23.6 / −20.0 / −20.0 meV). The liquid is an ideal solution of the SGTE liquids (no liquid data, as in the paper). The SGTE functions were extended down to 1 K to compute the 100–300 K ordering window (all solids share the same GHSER, so the extrapolation cancels between solid phases).
1155: Fig. 10e. Two routes for the same MLIP (MACE-MPA-0) (ptrh/out/calphad_mace_mpa_0/calphad_vs_hull.png, y axis 100–400 K / 1700–2400 K). Left: reference = SGTE PtRh-98Jac fcc+liquid and the paper's Table 7 (PFP solid, DFT dashed). Middle: hull route (liquid window of stages 01–07 + solids-only low-T re-assembly, noise filtered, ▼ = CE+MC). Right: CALPHAD route (this section's TDB evaluated with pycalphad on a 10 K × 0.005 grid, 2 K grid in the low-T window). CALPHAD-route ordering: fcc↔PtRh 176 K (x 0.46–0.52), fcc↔PtRh₃ 146 K, Pt₃Rh ≤ 106 K, eutectoids fcc↔PtRh+PtRh₃ 135 K (x 0.683) and fcc↔Pt₃Rh+PtRh 106 K. The solid–liquid side is ideal liquid + SGTE, so Pt 2041.5 K and Rh 2237 K are unchanged and the fcc+liquid band is at most Δx 0.045 wide (2170 K).
1166: Same input, ±35 K between routes. For MACE-MPA-0 the fcc↔PtRh ordering is 176 K by the CALPHAD route (Bragg–Williams-type CEF), 230 K by the hull route (defect cells + sublattice entropy) and 160 K by CE + canonical MC (short-range order included). This is comparable to the paper's PFP–DFT difference (258 vs 211 K) and smaller than the spread between MLIPs (GRACE-2L and NequIP-OAM-M give no ordered phase at all). It is 30 K below the paper's DFT version although the PtRh ordering energy is the same −11 meV/atom, because the temperature coefficient of MACE's fcc excess term (+2.6 T, negative excess vibrational entropy) stabilises fcc relatively at high temperature.
1167: Pitfall of the unpartitioned two-sublattice CEF. The disordered state of an ordered phase (equal occupation on both sublattices) competes with fcc as a separate phase; with the MACE parameters the fcc RK excess and the disordered D0₂₂ state become degenerate within a few J/mol at 2100–2150 K, and pycalphad's mapping returns spurious fcc+D0₂₂+liquid three-phase points. calphad_tdb.py relabels vertices with a sublattice occupation difference |Δy| < 0.05 as fcc. With the standard order–disorder partition (--model partition) PtRh rises to 210–214 K, but for the asymmetric (Pt,Rh)₀.₇₅(Pt,Rh)₀.₂₅ phase the disordered state is not a stationary point with end-member parameters alone, so the D0₂₂ order parameter decays continuously without a transition (Ansara–Dupin-type constrained interaction parameters would be needed). The table uses the paper's unpartitioned model.
1168: The solid–liquid side carries no MLIP information (as in the paper). The solid–liquid side with the MLIP's liquid TI is Fig. 10d (Pt 1480 K, Rh 1904 K; experiment 2041/2237 K).
1169: Melting points (11-09 to 10): the 2,048-atom TI of the end members inside the solids-only WorkChain melted Pt at the caps 2150, 1980 and 1850 K (NequIP even at 1850 K), so the liquid was extended down to 1500 K and crossed with 1400–1700 K sweeps. Rh: GRACE-2L 2032, NequIP-OAM-M 2050, MACE-MPA-0 1904 K (experiment 2237); Pt: 1490 / 1420 / 1480 K (experiment 2041, a short extrapolation just below 1500 K). QHA − TI is −40 to −100 meV/atom for fcc (1550–2050 K), which is why QHA said "does not melt". All three universal MLIPs underestimate Pt by 550–620 K and Rh by 190–330 K. The paper gives no PFP melting-point values, so no comparison is possible.

1174: Abbreviations and technical terms used on this page without explanation. The equations are in Appendix B and skills/phase-diagram/references/workflow.md.
1177: Machine-learning interatomic potential: a function fitted to DFT energies, forces and stresses that runs atomistic calculations (relaxation, phonons, molecular dynamics, thermodynamic integration) 10³–10⁶ times faster than DFT. In this project the MLIP stands in for DFT: every free energy that decides the phase diagram comes from it.
1178: A universal MLIP (foundation model) covers almost the whole periodic table with one model, trained on large DFT sets such as the Materials Project trajectories (MPtrj), OMat24 and sAlex. The 12 compared here: GRACE-FS/1L/2L, SevenNet-0/-MF-ompa, MACE-MPA-0, MatterSim-v1-1M/5M, NequIP-OAM-M/S, DPA4-Plus-OMat24, plus the system-specific ACE. Matbench Discovery is the standard 0 K stability benchmark.
1179: Atomic Cluster Expansion: an MLIP form that expands the atomic environment in a many-body basis. The Al–Li ACE used here is the system-specific potential of the pyiron workshop (trained on Al–Li only) and serves as the reference for the universal MLIPs. In LAMMPS it is pair_style pace, on the GPU pace/kk. GRACE is its graph-based universal descendant.
1180: CALculation of PHAse Diagrams: each phase's Gibbs energy G(T, x) is written with a few parameters (SGTE functions of the end members + Redlich–Kister excess + sublattice models) and the phase diagram follows from minimising the total G. The parameters are fitted to experiments or calculations (an assessment). Route A of this project takes the convex hull directly from the stage-05 free-energy table, so it does not require CALPHAD-type interpolation (section 6).
1181: Thermodynamic DataBase file (extension .tdb): the text format that holds CALPHAD parameters, made of elements (ELEMENT), temperature functions (FUNCTION, e.g. GHSERAL), phases with their sublattices (PHASE, CONSTITUENT) and parameters (PARAMETER G/L). Thermo-Calc, pycalphad and OpenCalphad read it. Here stage 05 (calphy PhaseDiagram / ftphase.records) exports TDBs, and the ESPEI fit (alli-mcmc.tdb) and the Pt–Rh Saengdeejing route (ptrh_mace_mpa_0.tdb) are stored as TDBs too. ORCHID-Diagrams distributes pycalphad-computed boundaries, not the TDBs themselves.
1182: The pure-element database of the Scientific Group Thermodata Europe (Dinsdale 1991): G(T) of each element's stable phase as polynomials above 298.15 K (GHSERxx), the reference state of every CALPHAD assessment. This project uses SGTE91 from espei.refdata; for Pt–Rh it was extrapolated down to 1 K for the 100–300 K ordering window (it cancels between solid phases).
1183: Polynomial for the excess Gibbs energy of a solution phase, G^ex = x_A x_B Σ_k L_k (x_A − x_B)^k with L_k = a_k + b_k T, added to the ideal mixing RT Σ x ln x. Used here for the liquid G(x) fit (fits={'liquid': 'rk'}) and for fcc in Pt–Rh. Fitting a G that still contains k_B T x ln x with a polynomial invents miscibility gaps, so only the excess is fitted.
1184: Compound Energy Formalism (sublattice model): an ordered phase is written with several sublattices (A,B)_p(A,B)_q, and G(y) is built from the end-member energies (A:B etc.) plus ideal mixing within each sublattice. The Neumann–Kopp approximation sets a mixed end member to the sum of the pure-element GHSER plus ΔH_f − TΔS_f. In the unpartitioned CEF the disordered state of the ordered phase competes with fcc as a separate phase (pitfall, Pt–Rh at the end of section 4).
1185: Quasi-harmonic approximation: phonons (phonopy / ALAMODE) at a few volumes, F(V, T) = E₀(V) + F_vib(V, T) minimised over V to give G(T, P). Anharmonicity (phonon–phonon scattering, diffusion) is absent, so it overstabilises solids near the melting point (−20 to −100 meV/atom in Ni–Al and Pt–Rh). Stage 03A of this project.
1186: Thermodynamic integration: the Hamiltonian is switched with λ from a reference system (solid: Einstein crystal, Frenkel–Ladd; liquid: Uhlenbeck–Ford model, UFM) to the MLIP, the free-energy difference is integrated, and reversible scaling then sweeps the temperature. calphy implements it with LAMMPS hybrid/scaled. It gives absolute free energies including anharmonicity. Solids need ≥ 2,000 atoms (256-atom cells come out 7 meV/atom too low). Stage 03B and the solid TI.
1187: Special quasirandom structure: atoms placed in a small cell so that its correlation functions match a random solid solution (icet, sqsgenerator, ATAT mcsqs). The solid-solution series here are 32–64-atom random or icet-SQS cells, with the configurational entropy added separately as ideal mixing (stages 02A, 04A). The configuration noise of a 32-atom cell is about 5 meV/atom.
1188: Cluster expansion + Monte Carlo: the configurational energy on a lattice is written as a linear sum of cluster correlations (ECI, enumerated and fitted with icet), and canonical or semi-grand-canonical (SGC, VCSGC) MC gives the finite-temperature configurational free energy, short-range order and order–disorder transitions directly. Indispensable instead of the defect-cell method when the ordering energy is below the configuration noise (5 meV; Pt–Rh). One of the route-B methods.
1189: Convex hull / common tangent: at each temperature the lower convex hull of all phases' G(x) points gives the two-phase regions as hull edges (common tangents) and the single-phase regions as vertices. Stage 06 takes the hull directly from the point set without interpolation functions, mixing point phases (compounds) with phases of finite width. At 0 K the hull of the formation energies is the ground-state line (the hull check of stage 01).
1190: Invariant reaction: a temperature at which three phases coexist in a binary (zero degrees of freedom). Eutectic L ↔ α + β, eutectoid α ↔ β + γ, peritectic L + α ↔ β, congruent melting. Stage 07 detects it as the temperature interval between grid points where the set of two-phase pairs changes (e.g. the Al–Li eutectic at 760–770 K), so the resolution is the grid step. The ORCHID comparison compares these temperatures and compositions with the literature medians.
1191: Solvus (solubility limit): the composition boundary of a terminal solid solution (e.g. fcc Al) in equilibrium with a compound or another solid solution. Here it follows from 32-atom random cells + ideal mixing, so the configuration noise (one atom on the dilute side = x 0.03) and the defect-cell spacing are its error. For Ag–Cu it was also checked with CE+MC and direct MC (fix atom/swap).
1192: Classical vs quantum level: calphy's TI is classical statistics (MD), so the quantum-harmonic QHA is lowered by F_q − F_cl to the same level (04B). Near the melting point (T ≫ Debye temperature) the difference is small, but it is essential in the 100–300 K ordering window of Pt–Rh. The correction is the same for all phases, so the ordering temperatures came out almost identical at the two levels.
1193: Free-energy model of thermal point defects: anti-sites and vacancies of an ordered phase (B2 NiAl) as independent dilute defects, so that off-stoichiometry is carried by equilibrium thermal defects rather than by constitutional ones. It removes the cusp at stoichiometry and the spurious same-phase segments (section 5).
1194: The literature-evidence database of Arróyave, Saal and Shin (arXiv:2610.41164, v2026.10): 73,542 invariant reactions and phase-region points extracted from 1,321 papers, pycalphad-computed boundaries of the SGTE binary assessments (ORCHID-Diagrams) and ESPEI datasets. It is a reference for comparison, not a free-energy method. This project compares each run's invariants with the literature medians (orchid_compare.py) and overlays the SGTE boundaries (sgte_diagrams.py).
1195: pycalphad is the Python library that reads TDBs and computes equilibria and phase diagrams (used here to check TDBs and for the Pt–Rh CALPHAD route, version 0.11.2). ESPEI generates TDB parameters from datasets and refines them by MCMC (route 2, which fitted Al–Li from ORCHID data alone). Both MIT-licensed.
1196: AiiDA is a workflow engine that records the provenance of every calculation automatically. A WorkChain describes stages 01–07 as one procedure (ftphase.txdiagram), a CalcJob is one job submitted to Slurm (QHA, calphy), and pk is the running number of a node in the database (e.g. pk 12176). A CalcJob with identical inputs is reused from the cache instead of being recomputed.
1197: LAMMPS is the molecular-dynamics code (calphy's engine). Kokkos is its GPU layer: pair styles with the /kk suffix (pace/kk, grace/kk, metatomic/kk) run on the GPU. ML-IAP (pair_style mliap unified) is the common entry point that runs pickled PyTorch models (MACE, SevenNet, MatterSim, NequIP) in the embedded Python of LAMMPS, removing the need for one forked LAMMPS per model.
1198: Units: this project's free energies are in eV/atom (1 eV/atom = 96.485 kJ/mol-atom), CALPHAD and TDBs use J/mol (per mole of atoms; beware of literature values per formula unit). 1 meV/atom ≈ 96.5 J/mol ≈ k_B T at 11.6 K. The statement "a 10 meV/atom offset shifts a melting point by ~100 K" uses this conversion.
